stage: development only; no study-01 test recording, study-02 fresh recording, synthetic test scene or new fresh recording was read
rule: Written after the diagnostic trials on development material (results-tone-forecaster-03/diagnosis) and before the formal development run. Candidates, all gated: the joint band check of study 02 with its tie fallback capped at 0.5 dB (the fallback switched off), 1, 2 and 3 dB; above the cap only no output is allowed. Development material: the eight study-01 development recordings, the 44 development synthetic scenes and the 8 new buzz scenes. A boost is a third-octave band 1 dB or more louder; a near-boost 0.5 dB or more; both are counted over development recordings (either horizon) plus late synthetic windows. Eligible only if: (a) the boosts go down: fewer boosts than joint + gate; (b) no more near-boosts than joint + gate; (c) no more whole-band boosts (whole 35-350 Hz band below -0.5 dB on a development recording) than joint + gate; (d) the tone gain over v2 is kept: the median, over development acoustic recordings with reference tones, of the tone-bin gain averaged over both horizons is at least v2 + gate's plus half of the amount by which joint + gate exceeds v2 + gate; (e) the median whole-band gain over development acoustic recordings, averaged over both horizons, is at least joint + gate's minus 0.1 dB; (f) the mean synthetic objective is at least joint + gate's minus 0.5 dB and its synthetic windows below -0.5 dB are no more than joint + gate has; (g) its own compute time per 10 ms block at the 99th percentile, worst run, is within 0.5 ms of joint + gate's in the same run (the capped check does the same work). Among eligible candidates, pick the one with the fewest boosts, then the fewest near-boosts, then the higher tone-bin median. If none is eligible, nothing is frozen: the joint check and v2 are unchanged, and there is nothing to test on fresh recordings.
